questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I specifically chose The University of Adelaide, because they provided courses that were highly relevant to my bachelor's degree in Cognitive Data Science and my career aspirations. As I am dreaming of working with AI governance, I chose the courses "AI & Human Life", "Cyber-politics" and "Introduction to Global Politics".

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My exchange experience has been incredibly valuable both personally and academically.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The University had arranged an introduction week, where we got the opportunity to meet other exchange students from around the world, and we got all the important information.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Great.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I was lucky to get a room in a shared house in a nice and quiet sub urb called Kensington Park. My roomies had made a post on a Facebook page, called something like "Flatmates in Adelaide". You can also use the website "
Flatmates.au
" to find off campus accommodation.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed living with locals from Adelaide - it was great to have personal guides and to meet their friends :)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't live in the housing provided by the uni.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Easy and great acces to get help at campus.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was a big "Ask Adelaide" desk at campus with staff that could help you with anything.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply in advance - and if you regret your choice, you can change your classes until August 11th.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was happy with all of my courses - they were very all relevant and had super interesting reading and great professors.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Similar to KU.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I really liked the assessment form - we were assessed on different parameters, both on how active you are in class, assignments, MC-tests, exams, etc.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
POLIS 3003 - Cyber-Politics: Politics & the Internet Revolution
PHIL 2053 - AI and Human Life: Ethics, Politics, Subjectivity
POLIS 1102 - Introduction to Global Politics
FILM 1006 - Hollywood Film

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Cyber-Politics! Everything was so well structured, the teachers were amazing and my classmates came from many different degrees or industries.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Flight tickets :) Make sure to book them as early as possible.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The University provided a bunch of different clubs and societies. There is something for everyone.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I did some writing for the PPE magazine (Politics, Philosophy and Economics).

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Just find something you like. It is a great opportunity to meet more people - both locals and other exchange students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The beautiful botanical garden next to uni! Wine trips to Barossa Valley or McLaren Vale! Hikes in the hills! The Central Market! Weeknd trip to Melbourne - rent a car and to Great Ocean Road.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy - Australians are very easy going and laid back.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Find a room in a shared house :)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The slang! And their accents were sometimes a little challenging to decode :)

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The beautiful nature surrounding Adelaide and the friendly people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Make sure to understand the assessment of each of your courses early on. It differs a lot from course to course, and it is your own responsibility to understand the deadlines etc.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Even more information on assessment.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The extremely interesting courses, all the beautiful people I've met and living in such a nice and perfect city for students.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I tore my ACL  a skiing accident in September in Mt. Hotham (1,5 month in), so I had to spend a great time focusing on recovery and making claims for my insurance.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I highly recommend an exchange semester in Adelaide - the university is like a small village with all faculties at the same place. It is nice to be a small group of students from Denmark (around 12) compared to the larger cities like Melbourne and Sydney. We got really close and spent a lot of time together.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
